title: Supplied Field Questionnaire and Scoring Key
paragraphs: Appendix A Supplied Field Questionnaire and Scoring Key The following reproduces the content of the supplied bilingual F1.0 form, with layout adapted for the thesis. The Markdown and HTML versions are archived under survey_instruments. They document the instrument supplied for this study; no independent translation-validation result is inferred. The wider platform's prebroadcast, echo-triggered, and weekly instrument proposals are not presented as questions administered in this eld wave. A.1 Information and Consent Wording Title: LOKLOK Media Listening & Trust Questionnaire (F1.0). Researcher: Sherif Rashwan LOKLOK social-media radio network research. Purpose: Understand how university students evaluate broadcast quality, source trust, and content diversity while listening during a car / Uber ride. Consent: Anonymous, voluntary, academic use only. No right/wrong answers; skip any item. Duration approximately 5 min. Condentiality: No identifying data; reported only in aggregate. The supplied form uses English explanatory prose with bilingual labels. These statements are reproduced as instrument wording, 250

APPENDIX A. SUPPLIED FIELD QUESTIONNAIRE AND SCORING KEY 251 not as certication that the separately supplied prole archive is anonymous. The discrepancy and implications for quotation and LLM use are addressed in Chapter 5. A.2 Section 0: About You 1. Age: open numerical response. 2. Gender: male; female. 3. Academic year: rst, second, third, or fourth. 4. Faculty: Mass Communication; Commerce; Engineering; Science; Other, specify. 5. University: select one of the following source-form categories:  October 6 University (O6U).  Cairo University 6th of October Branch.  Misr University for Science & Technology (MUST).  Modern University for Technology & Information (MTI).  Sadat Academy for Management Sciences 6th of October.  Higher Institutes of 6th of October City.  Other: specify. The form explicitly excludes Ahram Canadian University (ACU). Institution names are source-form labels, not independent verication of campus geography or ocial institutional nomenclature. 6. Listening context: Uber; private car; microbus; public transport.

APPENDIX A. SUPPLIED FIELD QUESTIONNAIRE AND SCORING KEY 252 A.3 Section A: Judging a Radio Broadcaster Think of a broadcaster/program you listened to during the ride. Rate 04: 0 = strongly disagree; 1 = disagree; 2 = neutral; 3 = agree; 4 = strongly agree. BR1 The broadcaster veries claims before going on air BR2 The broadcaster corrects mistakes quickly and openly BR3 The broadcaster stays fair when opinions clash BR4 The broadcaster exaggerates to gain attention SV1 Students whose opinion I respect follow and like this broadcaster SV2 Interacting with the audience shows the broadcaster cares SV3 A high social rating makes me trust the broadcaster more SV4 The broadcaster's popularity is a sign of its credibility IQ1 The content I heard is well-informed and substantial

APPENDIX A. SUPPLIED FIELD QUESTIONNAIRE AND SCORING KEY 253 IQ2 The broadcaster adds value beyond what I already know IQ3 The program content is consistently high quality A.4 Section B: The Broadcast Experience After listening, rate 17, from strongly disagree to strongly agree. PB1 I feel more condent about what I heard after listening PB2 The content exposed me to diverse perspectives I hadn't considered PB3 I trust this broadcaster more than others on similar topics PB4 The broadcast structure helped me understand the topic clearly PB5 Overall, the broadcast was of high quality and worth my time A.5 Section C: Overall Rating How would you rate this broadcast? Select 15: 1 = poor; 5 = excellent.

APPENDIX A. SUPPLIED FIELD QUESTIONNAIRE AND SCORING KEY 254 A.6 Scoring and Analysis Boundaries Reverse BR4 as 4 −BR4. BR, SV, and IQ are means of four, four, and three items respectively; the broadcaster-battery total used for alpha contains all 11 scored items. PB is the arithmetic mean of PB1PB5 on its original 17 scale. The star response remains a separate 15 variable. No missing item cells occur in the supplied 60 questionnaires, so the recheck does not impute values or exercise a missing-item prorating rule. The 04 and 17 anchors must not be interchanged. PB3 measures comparative trust, not intention to verify; PB4 measures structural clarity, not the inuence of a displayed BRS. SV3 directly concerns a high social rating, but even this item records perceived inuence rather than an experimentally identied badge eect. The HTML/Markdown form, scored CSV, and qualitative notes are dierent artifacts; ride mood and recorded quotations do not become additional questionnaire scale items simply because they can be linked.
